correctness.rationale: The counterexample is exact: the coefficient energy \(|x_1|^2+|x_1+x_2|^2\) dominates \(|x_1|^2=\|K^*x\|^2\), while the resulting frame operator satisfies \(Se_1=2e_1+e_2\notin R(K)\). Thus \((S|_{R(K)})^{-1}e_1\) is undefined when the inverse is correctly viewed on \(S(R(K))\). For the repair, \((K^\dagger)^*K^*x=x\) on \(R(K)\) gives \(\langle P_RSx,x\rangle\ge A\|K^\dagger\|^{-2}\|x\|^2\); bounded self-adjoint coercivity makes the compression invertible and both reconstruction identities follow by substitution.

originality.rationale: The published formula is genuinely ill-typed without range invariance, and the displayed three-dimensional example is an exact witness. Later literature explicitly distinguishes the invertible map \(S:R(K)\to S(R(K))\) or adds \(S(R(K))=R(K)\), but the checked sources do not give this concrete obstruction to Huang--Yang equation (2.10). The universal compression itself is close to a standard corollary of Huang--Yang Theorem 3.3(2): on \(R(K)\) the same coefficient family is an ordinary g-fusion frame, whose subspace frame operator is the compression. That prior ingredient materially narrows the novelty claim, but it does not itself expose the domain error or supply the counterexample. Best-of-knowledge originality is therefore retained for the correction/obstruction, not for the abstract existence of a positive invertible compression alone.
residual_risks: The compression theorem by itself is largely a standard subspace-frame consequence of Huang--Yang Theorem 3.3(2); novelty is not claimed for that abstract frame-theoretic mechanism alone.
An unindexed erratum or informal correction could already contain the same explicit domain objection.
